description: [being built] The X-Ezgh-Caller header (contracts/identity-and-authz.md, "Delegated checks"; docs/delegated-calls-design.md, "The caller reference"). valid: each reference and its canonical header, both ways: the kits' formatter (Go delegation.Reference.String, service-kit formatCallerReference) writes exactly header, and their parser (delegation.Parse, parseCallerReference) gives back reference. invalid: headers every parser refuses, with the message it gives (the parser checks, in order: at most 512 bytes; printable ASCII with no whitespace; the six keys in order; then each value in key order; then that no ID looks like a credential: starts with ezgh_ or is a service credential's key_id). classifierOnly cases are a request's whole set of X-Ezgh-Caller values (none, or two): the receiver's request handling refuses them before parsing. A receiver answers every refusal 400 invalid_caller_reference with the message as the issue at X-Ezgh-Caller; org-api answers 400 invalid_request with an issue at reference. The grammar caps a canonical header at about 330 bytes, so the 512-byte limit only bounds what a parser reads.

valid.name: a session (better-auth text IDs, a UUID organization)
a federated console session acting as a bot
an OAuth access token (the token's ID, not the grant's)
an SSO token by prefixed ID
the longest canonical header: 64-character IDs, 12-digit at, two 32-letter namespaces (the grammar caps a header well under 512 bytes)
the shortest: one-character IDs and a two-letter namespace
